articles: A gentle start to your movement practice
gentle-start

Bring comfortable clothes and tell your coach what a good week would feel like. Your first session is a conversation as well as a chance to move.

We keep the pace unhurried. You can pause, ask questions, or change an exercise. Share any access needs before your appointment so the studio can prepare.
Making room for a regular routine
regular-routine

A routine is easier to maintain when it fits your day. Choose a time you can reach without rushing, and leave a little space afterwards.

Between sessions, notice what feels useful. Bring those observations to your next appointment. These fictional showcase notes are general information, not individual health advice.
What to expect in the studio
studio-visit

The Gerji studio is a quiet space for one-to-one coaching. Your booking confirmation includes the appointment time and arrival details.

Tell us if you need step-free access or a different arrangement. If your plans change, use the cancellation or rescheduling link in your confirmation.
Getting ready for your first salon visit
first-salon-visit

Bring photos of styles you like, and tell your stylist about your current routine. We will discuss time, care, and the service you booked before starting.

If you have sensitivities or specific product preferences, mention them when you arrive. A clear conversation helps us plan a comfortable visit.
Finding a care routine that fits
care-routine

Your hair care routine should suit your schedule and preferences. Ask your stylist which steps are essential and which are optional.

Write down the products you already use, and bring your questions. These fictional studio notes do not replace a personal consultation or medical advice.
Meet the spaces at Bole Bloom
studio-spaces

The main studio has room for everyday appointments, while the quiet styling room offers a calmer setting. Choose the available location when booking.

Your confirmation shows where to go. If you need a quieter appointment or extra assistance, contact the team before your visit.
collections: Details that make a visit comfortable

articles: Preparing for your first fitting
first-fitting

Bring the garment, the shoes you expect to wear with it, and an idea of when you need it. The fitting is a chance to discuss how the garment should feel as well as how it looks.

We will explain the proposed adjustments and timing before work begins. Leave room for a second fitting when the alteration needs one.
Small details, considered carefully
considered-details

A sleeve, hem, or fastening can change the way a garment feels throughout the day. Tell us where you notice discomfort when you sit, walk, or reach.

We can discuss practical adjustments in the appointment. These fictional atelier notes illustrate the kind of questions that help a fitting.
Caring for a garment after alterations
garment-care

Check the original care label and ask whether the alteration changes how the garment should be pressed or stored. Keep any spare buttons or fabric with it.

If something feels different after the first wear, make a note and contact the atelier. Bring the garment back rather than trying an unfamiliar adjustment yourself.
Your first conversation session
first-conversation

Bring a situation you would like to handle more comfortably: greeting a neighbour, asking a question, or explaining your work. Your teacher will use that goal to shape the practice.

You do not need to arrive with perfect answers. The session gives you room to try, pause, and ask for help.
Practice between appointments
between-sessions

A short, regular practice can be more manageable than a long session once a week. Choose one useful phrase and try it in a real or imagined conversation.

Bring difficult moments to your next lesson. We can practise a different way to say the same thing and discuss where it might be useful.
Learning in a welcoming space
learning-space

Our fictional language house has spaces for individual conversation and small learning groups. Booking details show the selected session and location.

Tell the team about access needs or materials that help you learn. We can discuss a suitable arrangement before your first visit.
Preparing for a consultation
preparing-consultation

Bring a list of your questions and the medicines or supplements you currently take. Your appointment confirmation includes the clinic location and arrival information.

If you need an interpreter or accessibility support, contact the clinic in advance. These fictional showcase notes are general appointment information, not medical advice.
Making your questions easier to remember
remembering-questions

It can help to write down what changed, when you first noticed it, and what you want to understand. Bring those notes to the consultation.

Ask the clinician to explain anything that is unclear. If you need urgent medical help, use the appropriate local emergency service rather than waiting for a routine booking.
A calm arrival at the clinic
calm-arrival

Allow time to find the clinic and complete the arrival steps described in your confirmation. Tell reception if you need assistance or a quieter place to wait.

If you cannot attend, use your confirmation link to cancel or reschedule. This helps the clinic make the time available to another visitor.
